failures.criterion: Enter answers the selected question: it opens a decision block's note field AND puts the reader in it, as this change's own documentation says (docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/keyboard.md: `Enter` - Answer the selected ask (moves into its answer box, opening the note field of a decision block first)), and as Inbox.tsx's Enter binding intends (`inAnswerHand(NOTE_DISCLOSURE_SELECTOR)?.click();` then `inAnswerHand("[data-ask-answer]")?.focus()`).
failures.evidence: Red row `Enter opens the selected decision block's note field and puts the focus in it` in packages/dispatch/e2e/inbox-reading-pane.e2e.ts, commit d542d2dac754880a47917be4fdf99a38d89126ef, pushed. Command: `source /legion/harness/env.sh && cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- e2e/inbox-reading-pane.e2e.ts --project=chromium -g "note field"`. At a87c4269 it fails: `expect(locator).toBeFocused() failed; Locator: getByTestId('inbox-pane').locator('[data-dispatch-ask-block="rollout-order"]').locator('article[data-testid^=ask-]').locator('[data-ask-answer]'); Received: inactive`. A diagnostic probe printed the whole sequence on the page: after ONE Enter the disclosure reads aria-expanded=true and the card holds one [data-ask-answer] box, and document.activeElement is BODY; after a SECOND Enter the focus is that box. So the field opens and the reader is not in it, and every keystroke after it is still the Inbox's keymap - `j` walks the list while the reader believes they are writing an answer. Why the unit row misses it: `fireEvent` flushes React synchronously, so the textarea exists by the time `focus()` runs; in a browser the click's state update has not rendered yet, so `focus()` finds nothing. The fix needs the focus after the render (the box's own autofocus on open, or a focus the disclosure's own effect takes), and the red row above is the check.

The third is new this round: `e2e/nav.e2e.ts:14 sidebar shows Inbox, Pinned, one row per project with its open-ask badge, and Settings - never an issue row - on desktop and in the phone drawer @phone`. It reproduces with its file run alone (1 failed, 1 passed), so it is no shared-CPU failure: `expect(received).toEqual(expected)` with `Array [ "?pinned=true", - "/api/v1/issues/CORE-2" ]` - the reading column no longer makes the one per-issue read the row was taught to expect in round 1. Nothing of the head is lost with it: ReadingPaneHead.tsx:108 takes the priority from the ask row (`<PriorityControl issueKey={ask.issue_key} priority={ask.priority} />`), and e2e/inbox.e2e.ts:768, which drives that control through the pane head, is green in the same run. So this is the refactor making the column read less, and the row's expectation is now stale and this change's to correct (with the saved read named in the body, since it is an improvement worth stating). It is a failure of the round rather than a defect of the product: the implementer's own round ran 7 spec files and 88 rows, not the project, so nothing of theirs could have shown it.
